content:
Mia: heads up — seeing steady memory growth on long streaming chats with tool loops. not a sudden spike, just a slow climb in RSS and KV residency after ~25-40 min. attaching pprof + short heap snapshot below.

Sam: can you paste the pprof top lines? also which runtime binary/flags were used?

Mia: runtime: inference-server v2.3.1, flags: --kv-enabled --streaming=true --kv-compact-interval=10m. repro is toolloop stress with 8 parallel sessions, ~1k tokens/min each. pprof heap top: 
```
(pprof) top15
0.45GB  40.2% 40.2%  kv.PagePool.alloc  
0.22GB  19.6% 59.8%  session.SessionState.refs  
0.11GB   9.8% 69.6%  page.SlabFragmenter.split  
0.09GB   8.0%77.6%  kv.Cache.put  
```
not huge single allocs — looks like many small page fragments.

Raj: interesting. that PagePool.alloc figure suggests pages are being kept alive, not freed. do you see cache eviction logs? 

Mia: eviction logs show regular churn but effective residency increases: 
```
I-2026-03-18T14:00:00Z evict: candidate_count=128 evicted=64 tail_trim=32
I-2026-03-18T14:10:00Z evict: candidate_count=132 evicted=66 tail_trim=34
...
```
we're evicting, but total page_count still increases over time.

Ophelia: hypothesis: fragmentation + partial references from active sessions prevents whole pages from being reclaimed. pages get split to satisfy small KV slices for tool tokens, leaving orphaned fragments. compaction currently only runs on eviction, not proactively. :thinking: 

Sam: can you repro with KV debug tracing on? add --kv-trace=page_free,page_split and run for ~1h. that'll show refs preventing page_free.

Mia: started a run with trace enabled. initial diff shows many page_split events with no immediately following page_free for the parent page id. small example: 
```
page_split pid=0x7f3b id=1234 -> child_ids=[1235,1236] sizes=[4k,12k]
kv_ref_inc pid=1235 session=s-42 key=tool_out_17
# later... no page_free for pid=1234 after 10m
```

Raj: that aligns with a bug we saw earlier where session.SessionState holds transient references to sub-slices but the parent page metadata isn't updated to clear ownership. if true, compaction should detect and merge fragments back or at least free empty slabs.

Ophelia: quick mitigations: (1) add a periodic compaction pass that walks low-util pages and coalesces/returns fully-free slabs to system, (2) increase frequency of KV quick-sweep (currently 10m) to 1m for long-run experiments, (3) add a safety TTL for tiny fragments to be promoted to separate frees if unreferenced for X seconds.

Sam: agree. for the experiment: bump --kv-compact-interval=1m and enable the compaction patch on a canary build, run stress for 2 hours. collect pprof every 15m and compare PagePool.alloc curve.

Mia: I'm on it. started canary with compaction and 1m interval on a 3-node canary pool. will post graphs soon.

perf-bot: ALERT: canary 3-node pool (canary-2026-03-18-15:00) started with kv-compact=1m and compaction=true. pprof dumps scheduled every 15m.

Mia: first 30m look promising — RSS slope flattened vs baseline. still seeing small residual growth (~3-4MB/hr) vs ~25MB/hr baseline. saving full heap diff for Raj.

Raj: thanks. next steps: (A) instrument parent->child page refs so compactor can reconcile ownership, (B) add unit test for split/merge lifecycle with simulated toolloop ref patterns, (C) consider eager coalescing on session end. I'll open a PR for the tracing helpers.

Ophelia: add an integration test harness that simulates many small tool outputs to exercise fragmentation path. we should also review kernel selection impacts (small alloc hot path) but that's follow-up.

Mia: noted. created ticket INF-4659 with experiment logs + baseline graphs, attaching trace and pprof. assigning to Raj + Ophelia for fixes.

Sam: thanks team. if compaction + TTL reduces slope to near-zero in extended runs, we can roll to prod. keep an eye on latency impact from more frequent compaction.

Mia: will run a latency sweep next. thanks all :thumbsup:
